extracted.intended_audience: School and university officials, Title IX coordinators, campus legal counsel, and institutional administrators responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for educational institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and higher education) to implement and comply with Title IX final regulations (particularly §§106.6, 106.8, 106.30, 106.44, 106.45). Covers coordination, notice, procedures, evidence standards, and interaction with State and other Federal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of conflicting State or local law (§106.6(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent of a conflict between State or local law and Title IX as implemented by §§106.30, 106.44, and 106.45, the obligation to comply with those sections is not obviated or alleviated by any State or local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added §106.6(h) to make explicit that where there is an actual, direct conflict, Title IX/regulations preempt State law; recipients may, however, decline Federal funds to avoid Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of complying with stricter State law
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations prohibits a recipient from complying with State laws that impose stricter requirements (e.g., stricter reporting requirements, timelines, broader definitions of sexual harassment, or requirements to investigate conduct outside an education program or activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State law contains stricter provisions, recipients may follow those stricter rules; final regs were revised (e.g., §106.45(b)(3)(i)) to clarify mandatory Title IX dismissals are limited to Title IX purposes and do not preclude other institutional action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal only for Title IX purposes (§106.45(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismissal of a formal complaint under §106.45(b)(3)(i) is only for Title IX purposes and does not preclude action under another provision of the recipient's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may continue to respond to conduct under other policies even when Title IX requires dismissal for Title IX jurisdictional reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape shield protections (§106.45(b)(6)(i)-(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence about the complainant's sexual predisposition or prior sexual behavior are not relevant, unless offered to prove someone else committed the conduct or concern specific prior incidents with the respondent and are offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is a robust limitation on admitting evidence of prior sexual behavior; where State law conflicts with this rape-shield rule (e.g., Kentucky), Title IX regulations will preempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may adopt the preponderance of the evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not prohibit recipients from using the preponderance of the evidence standard; recipients are free to adopt it, and the Department disagrees that the regs conflict with State laws that require that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the same standard for employee and student complaints is permissible and may level the evidentiary burden across respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform evidentiary standard across employee and student complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing problematic with requiring that the same standard be used for complaints against employees as complaints against students; recipients may choose to apply the same standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying the same standard can address power-differential concerns where employees may have advantages over students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Clery Act and VAWA
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations do not conflict with the Clery Act or VAWA, including geographic requirements and the standard of evidence; definitions from VAWA (dating violence, domestic violence, stalking) are incorporated into §106.30's definition of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients subject to Clery/VAWA must be able to comply with both those statutes/regulations and these Title IX regulations; the Department discusses Clery Act interaction elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution is optional and cannot be mandated (§106.45(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations allow but do not require recipients to provide an informal resolution process; a recipient may not require parties to participate in informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If State law prohibits informal resolution (mediation), a recipient need not offer informal resolution. §106.45(b)(9) leaves recipients flexibility to adopt, structure, or decline informal resolution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and authorization of a Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate and 'authorize' at least one employee as the 'Title IX Coordinator' and must refer to that person by that title; the Coordinator must be authorized to coordinate the recipient's obligations under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'authorize' language is intended to prevent token or 'in name only' designations; the recipient remains responsible for ensuring Title IX obligations are met whether tasks are delegated or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and dissemination of Title IX Coordinator contact information and non-discrimination notice (§106.8(b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information (office address, telephone number, email) and the notice of non-discrimination, and must prominently display them on the recipient's website and in handbooks or catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department moved the list of persons to be notified into §106.8(a) and emphasizes use of websites/handbooks/catalogs as reasonable modern dissemination methods; contact info must be accessible (including for non-business hours reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Any person may report using Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (not only the alleged victim) may use the Title IX Coordinator's contact information to report sex discrimination, including sexual harassment; reports may be made at any time, including during non-business hours by phone, email, or mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad reporting access is intended to ensure accessibility even when the Coordinator is located in an administrative building; recipients should ensure practical access methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to delegate Title IX Coordinator duties; recipient remains responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations restricts tasks that a Title IX Coordinator may delegate to other personnel; however, the recipient is responsible for ensuring obligations imposed on the Title IX Coordinator are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked for lists of non-delegable duties; the Department declined to impose such lists but will hold recipients accountable for compliance overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandated minimum Title IX staffing levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require a minimum number of Title IX staff (e.g., 'at least one full-time dedicated' employee for certain enrollment sizes) or to mandate that a Coordinator be full-time or dedicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must determine staffing based on capacity to comply; if one Coordinator cannot coordinate compliance for a large recipient, the recipient may need additional personnel, but this is left to recipient discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of multiple or deputy Title IX Coordinators and their authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may designate multiple Title IX Coordinators and may designate 'deputy' or 'assistant' coordinators; such employees may be authorized to act on behalf of the recipient and notice to them conveys actual knowledge to the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deputy/assistant coordinators located on satellite campuses can improve accessibility; authorization should include the ability to institute corrective measures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator location/accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Title IX Coordinator is located in an office or building that restricts or impliedly restricts access only to certain students (e.g., a women's center), that placement could violate §106.8(a) by failing to 'authorize' the Coordinator to comply with all duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator contact methods must allow intake from any complainant regardless of sex; physical location should not impede access for any complainant or reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated notice/publication distribution approach (removal of 34 CFR 106.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed 34 CFR 106.9 and incorporated/modifed many of its provisions into §106.8(b); rather than requiring 'specific, continuing steps' the final regs emphasize posting on websites and including notices in handbooks and catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes technology (websites) provides efficient notice; other Title IX provisions (e.g., §§106.21, 106.51) continue to prohibit discriminatory practices even if explicit publication wording changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with State procedural fairness standards where they align (e.g., Washington APA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many procedural protections described by some State laws (freedom from bias for presiding officers, notice procedures, opportunity to respond, representation, cross-examination rules, prohibition on investigator serving as presiding officer, written orders, appeals) mirror requirements in the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where State procedural rules mirror the final regulations they generally do not conflict; the Department notes recipients can often comply with both sets of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to decline Federal funds to avoid Title IX obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not wish to be subject to Title IX and these final regulations, the recipient may choose not to accept Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit recognition that compliance with Title IX is a condition of federal financial assistance; choosing not to accept funds removes the Title IX obligation but has significant institutional consequences.
